findings.title: Live SQL path still builds DuckDB commands and reports invalid SQL
findings.body: Dashboard and alerting server-side expressions still enter through UnmarshalSQLCommand/NewSQLCommand, not ExpressionQueryReader. NewSQLCommand always calls sql.TablesList, which interpolates the user query into SELECT json_serialize_sql('...') and calls RunCommands. That now fails only because the new DB stub returns an error, and the failure is turned into BadRequest sql-invalid-sql with public text "error reading SQL command". Callers are told the SQL is invalid rather than that SQL expressions were disabled, and TablesList logs the raw query and the constructed command at error level on every attempt. The RCE/LFI closure on this path is entirely the stub; the old injection string is still built for every SQL expression. Reject in NewSQLCommand before TablesList, with an explicit disabled error, and do not assemble or log a DuckDB command.

findings.title: Disabled SQL expressions are reported as not implemented
findings.body: When QueryTypeSQL is read, the new gate always fails and returns "sqlExpressions is not implemented". The feature was implemented and is being turned off because of CVE-2024-9264; the feature flag is still present and documented as the switch for it. Clients and support will treat this as an unfinished feature rather than a security disable, and the message does not match the legacy path's "error reading SQL command" either.

findings.title: No regression test that SQL expressions cannot run
findings.body: This change is the in-repo fix for a critical RCE/LFI bug, but it adds no test that UnmarshalSQLCommand/NewSQLCommand reject SQL expressions, that ExpressionQueryReader rejects QueryTypeSQL even when FlagSqlExpressions is on, or that RunCommands/QueryFramesInto do not execute caller SQL. The only verification cited is manual. A later edit that fills in the DB stub or "fixes" enableSqlExpressions can re-open execution with nothing in CI failing.
